newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel - unemployment has no direct impact on EMU. [CORRECTED 15:49 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Waigel - unemployment has no direct impact on EMU. [CORRECTED 15:49 GMT]

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Tuesday that current labour market developments would not have a direct impact on the timetable for entry to Europe's planned single currency.

Speaking at a bank opening in Berlin (corrects from 'trade union conference in Berlin'), Waigel also acknowleged for the first time that average jobless levels in 1997 could exceed the government's previous forecast of 4.2 million.

Waigel said (corrects from 'told the conference') that stubbornly high German unemployment would affect the federal budget but there would be "no direct influence on the timetable for introducing the euro," Europe's planned single currency.
"We cannot rule out that unemployment levels will be higher than stated in the (government's) annual economic report," he said.

He was speaking just hours (corrects by removing the reference to a conference) after the Federal Labour Office reported that March unemployment fell a seasonally adjusted 15,000 to 4.3 million due to warm weather that gave an unexpected boost to the building sector.

Independent economists said the slight fall in March unemployment did not represent a turnaround on the labour market and high jobless levels will mean the government will have difficulty capping spending, challenging its efforts to qualify for European economic and monetary union.
